frequency_question: How often do structural frictions (such as compulsory conciliation, legal injunctions, or last-minute mandatory arbitration orders) completely prevent a threatened indefinite strike by a major federation within the stated window?
membership_rule: Includes industry-wide strike calls by recognized multi-union federations in heavily regulated economies where statutory conciliation or prohibition mechanisms exist. Excludes single-employer strikes or wildcat strikes without formal federation structures.
window: Any multi-week notice period leading up to a threatened nationwide indefinite strike.

cases.name: All-India Bank Employees Association / UFBU threatened strike (Nov 2022)
Central Trade Unions general strike notice (Mar 2022)
UFBU strike notice over five-day work week (Mar 2024)

coverage_note: 6 named prominent recent cases in the relevant jurisdiction and sector; believed representative of the friction-to-aversion ratio.
known_gaps: Excludes minor regional or single-bank subset strikes that did not involve the national umbrella federation.
skeleton: Not applicable; direct enumeration of relevant sector-wide federation strike calls used.
multiplier: 6 cases evaluated, 1 resulted in actual indefinite strike execution within window, 5 averted by structural/conciliation friction.
validity_reason: Labor laws and institutional conciliation mechanisms remain stable over multi-year periods barring major legislative overhaul.
